title: Supporting details and locating facts
blurb: Tell major from minor details, pick the detail that really supports a claim, and find stated facts with every qualifier matched.
question: A HESI A2 passage says a city's free helmet program gave out 4,200 helmets and that child head injuries fell from 48 a year to 29. The question asks: 'Which detail best supports the idea that the program worked?' Why is '4,200 helmets were given out' a trap, even though it is true?

teach.body: Formally, supporting details are the facts, examples, statistics, reasons, descriptions and anecdotes that explain or prove a main idea. Major details support the main idea directly; minor details support a major detail. A question that begins 'According to the passage' asks for something stated, often in different words. Plain English: the main idea is the claim, the details are the proof, and detail questions ask you to find one piece of proof exactly.

(1) Two years ago, the city of Linden began giving free bicycle helmets to children. Since then, fewer young riders have arrived at the emergency room with head injuries.

(2) The program has handed out 4,200 helmets, most of them at school safety fairs. Volunteers fit each helmet on the spot, because a helmet that sits too far back on the head protects far less. Families who cannot attend a fair can pick one up at any fire station.

(3) Before the program, Linden's hospital treated about 48 children a year for bike-related head injuries. Last year it treated 29. Adult riders, who were not part of the program, showed no change.

root.label: Main idea
root.sub: Free helmets cut child head injuries

teach.caption: A minor detail explains a major detail; it does not prove the main idea by itself.

teach.h: Detail stems and what they want
head: Stem
What it wants
rows: Which detail supports the idea that...?

teach.h: Scenario: Sofia works three detail stems
items: 'According to the passage, why do volunteers fit each helmet?' Scan paragraph 2: a helmet that sits too far back protects far less. Not 'because the helmets are free'.
'Which detail best supports the idea that the program worked?' Results live in paragraph 3: injuries fell from 48 to 29. '4,200 helmets were given out' is on topic but shows effort, not results.
'How many children were treated for bike head injuries last year?' 29, not 48: the qualifier 'last year' rules out the before figure.
Sofia Ramirez, applying to a PN program, finishes all three in about three minutes because she scans for the stem's key word, then reads the whole sentence around it.

steps.label: Scan
steps.sub: Find the word or a synonym

teach.body: Most wrong options in locate items are real details from the passage. They fail because they answer a slightly different question: weekday instead of Saturday, the old figure instead of the current one, children instead of adults, length instead of depth. Questions also paraphrase: the passage says 'homebound seniors', the question says 'older residents who cannot leave their homes'. Scan for meaning, not just the identical word.

teach.h: Why real details are wrong answers

children.label: Weekday hours for a Saturday question
The figure before a later change

teach.text: Watch for: a detail from the wrong paragraph; a number that belongs to a different group or time (48 before, 29 after); a detail that is on topic but does not support the claim asked about; a restatement of the claim itself offered as its proof; and words copied from the passage with the meaning changed. Finding the topic word is not the finish line: the qualifier is.

teach.body: Marcus Bell, applying to a surgical technology program, reads a passage saying a clinic opened with three exam rooms, moved to a building with eleven, and later converted two into a lab. Asked how many exam rooms it has today, he nearly picks 11, the figure for the new building. He reads on, sees the 2023 change and answers 9.

items: Supporting details are facts, examples, statistics, reasons, descriptions and anecdotes that prove the main idea.
Major details support the main idea directly; minor details support a major detail.
'Which detail supports X?' wants evidence for X, not just a detail on the same topic.
Scan for the stem's key word or a synonym, then read the whole sentence around it.
Match every qualifier: group, time, unit, before vs after. Most wrong options are real details that answer a different question.

summary: You can now tell major from minor supporting details and choose the detail that actually proves a given idea. You can also locate stated facts by scanning for key words and synonyms and confirm every qualifier so that a real but wrong detail does not catch you.

A.q:
Read the passage.

(1) Many hospitals now let parents stay overnight with children who are admitted.

(2) Nurses at one children's hospital say the change has helped young patients cope. Children whose parents stayed asked for pain medicine less often during the night, and several families said their child slept better. The hospital added fold-out chairs to every room in 2021.

Which detail from the passage best supports the idea that overnight stays help young patients cope?
options: Children with a parent present asked for pain medicine less often.
The hospital added fold-out chairs to every room in 2021.
Many hospitals now let parents stay overnight with children.
Nurses say the change has helped young patients cope.
A.why: Fewer requests for pain medicine at night is evidence that children coped better when a parent stayed.

whyNot.1: On topic but not support: the chairs show how the hospital made room, not that children coped better.
whyNot.2: This introduces the topic; it is not evidence that the stays help.
whyNot.3: This restates the claim itself; it does not prove it.

A.q:
Read the passage.

The Arlo River runs 210 miles from the Brenner Hills to Lake Tuck. For most of its course it is shallow, with an average depth of 12 feet. Near the Carver Dam, however, the channel reaches 60 feet. The dam itself, completed in 1958, stands 45 feet tall.

According to the passage, how deep is the Arlo River near the Carver Dam?
options: 12 feet
45 feet
60 feet
210 feet
A.why: The third sentence says that near the Carver Dam the channel reaches 60 feet.

whyNot.0: 12 feet is the average depth over most of the river.
whyNot.1: 45 feet is the height of the dam, not the depth of the river.
whyNot.3: 210 is the river's length in miles.

A.q: A passage's main idea is that a clinic's new evening hours have made care easier for working parents. Which detail is a minor detail that supports another detail rather than the main idea directly?
options: The clinic now stays open until 8 p.m. on weekdays.
Two nurses rotate to staff the new evening hours.
Visits by working parents rose by a third after the change.
Parents can now bring children in without leaving work.
A.why: Who staffs the evening hours explains how the late hours work; it supports the 'open until 8 p.m.' detail, not the claim that care is easier for parents.

whyNot.0: Major detail: the late hours are the change that makes care easier.
whyNot.2: Major detail: rising visits are direct evidence for the main idea.
whyNot.3: Major detail: it states the benefit to working parents directly.

B.q:
Read the passage.

(1) Pharmacists at Greenway Health now call every patient who starts a new blood pressure medicine.

(2) The call comes about a week after the first dose. The pharmacist asks about side effects such as dizziness and checks whether the patient has been taking the pills as directed. Patients who report problems are offered a same-week appointment.

According to the passage, what happens when a patient reports a problem during the call?
options: The pharmacist changes the medicine on the call
The patient stops the pills for one week
The pharmacist calls back a week later
The patient is offered a visit that week
B.why: 'Offered a same-week appointment' is restated as 'offered a visit that week'. Detail answers are often paraphrased.

whyNot.0: Unsupported: nothing says the pharmacist changes the medicine.
whyNot.1: Unsupported: the passage never tells patients to stop their pills.
whyNot.2: Distortion: 'a week' is when the first call comes, not a follow-up call.

B.q:
Read the passage.

The Rosewood Clinic opened in 2012 with three exam rooms. In 2018, it moved to a larger building on Pine Street, where it had eleven exam rooms. In 2023, two of those rooms were converted into a laboratory. The clinic hired its first full-time pharmacist in 2020.

According to the passage, how many exam rooms does the clinic have now?
B.why: The clinic had eleven exam rooms after 2018, and in 2023 two became a laboratory: 11 − 2 = 9.

whyNot.0: Three was the number when the clinic opened in 2012.
whyNot.2: Eleven was the number before the 2023 conversion.
whyNot.3: This adds the two converted rooms instead of subtracting them.

B.q:
Read the passage.

Route 12 buses leave Central Station every 20 minutes from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. on weekdays, then every 30 minutes until 7:00 p.m. On weekends, buses run every 45 minutes from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

How often do Route 12 buses leave Central Station at 11:00 a.m. on a Saturday?
options: Every 20 minutes
Every 45 minutes
Every 30 minutes
Every 60 minutes
B.why: Saturday is a weekend day, and weekend buses run every 45 minutes from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., which includes 11:00 a.m.

whyNot.0: Every 20 minutes is the weekday morning rush schedule.
whyNot.2: Every 30 minutes is the weekday schedule after 9:00 a.m.

C.q:
Read the passage.

The Hartwell Nursing Program admits students twice a year. Applications for the fall class are due March 1, and applications for the spring class are due September 15. Every applicant must submit a HESI A2 score from the past two years. Applicants who earned a B or higher in anatomy and physiology receive priority. Interviews for the fall class are held in April; interviews for the spring class are held in October.

Jasmine is applying for the spring class. According to the passage, in which month are interviews for her class held?
options: March
April
September
October
C.why: The last sentence says interviews for the spring class are held in October.

whyNot.0: March 1 is the fall application deadline.
whyNot.1: April is when fall-class interviews are held.
whyNot.2: September 15 is the spring application deadline, not the interview month.

C.q:
Read the passage.

Volunteers at the Eastgate Food Bank sort donations on Tuesdays and pack boxes on Thursdays. Deliveries to homebound seniors go out every Friday morning. The warehouse is closed on weekends, but donations can be left in the bin by the side door.

On which day are food boxes brought to older residents who cannot leave their homes?
options: Tuesday
Thursday
Friday
Saturday
C.why: The question paraphrases 'homebound seniors'. The passage says deliveries to them go out every Friday morning.

whyNot.0: Tuesday is when donations are sorted.
whyNot.1: Thursday is when boxes are packed, the step before delivery.
whyNot.3: The warehouse is closed on weekends; only donations can be dropped off.

C.q:
Read the notice.

Bring unused or expired medicines to the Elm Street fire station on Saturday, May 10, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Pills, patches and liquids are accepted; needles and inhalers are not. The service is free, and no questions are asked.

Which question can NOT be answered using the notice?
options: Is parking at the station free?
Will the drop-off accept inhalers?
What time does the drop-off end?
Is there a charge for the service?
C.why: The notice says the service is free but says nothing about parking, so a parking fee cannot be determined from it.

whyNot.2: Answered: the drop-off runs until 2 p.m.

reteach.title: Finding a friend at a stadium
reteach.question: Your friend texts: 'Section 214, row K, seat 9.' You do not read every seat number in the stadium. What do you do instead, and how is that like a HESI A2 locate item?

blocks.body: You follow the signs to the 200 level (the passage), walk to Section 214 (the right paragraph), find row K (the sentence) and count to seat 9 (the exact detail). If you stop at row K in Section 241, you are in a real seat, just the wrong one: that is the 'real detail, wrong qualifier' trap. Scanning is that same narrowing search through a passage.

blocks.text: Section 241 has a row K and a seat 9 too. Check every part of the address, just as you check every qualifier in the question.

explain.body: Major details support the main idea directly. Minor details explain, illustrate or add color to a major detail. Ask: does this sentence prove the main point, or does it explain another detail?

test.q:
Read the passage.

(1) Walking is one of the easiest ways for adults to stay active.

(2) It needs no special equipment beyond comfortable shoes. It can be done almost anywhere, from a park to a shopping mall on a rainy day. Many malls open their doors early so that walkers can circle the halls before the stores open.

Which sentence from the passage is a minor detail?
options: It needs no special equipment beyond comfortable shoes.
It can be done almost anywhere, from a park to a mall.
Many malls open early so walkers can circle the halls.
Walking is one of the easiest ways for adults to stay active.
test.why: Malls opening early explains the 'mall on a rainy day' example; it supports a major detail (walk almost anywhere), not the main idea directly.

whyNot.0: Major detail: needing no equipment directly shows walking is easy.
whyNot.1: Major detail: being possible almost anywhere directly shows walking is easy.
whyNot.3: This is the main idea, not a detail.

explain.body: The right answer is evidence FOR the idea in the stem. Reject a detail that is merely on the same topic, a detail that supports a different point, and a sentence that restates the claim without proving it.

test.q:
Read the passage.

(1) Views of nature may do more than please the eye.

(2) In one study, surgical patients whose windows faced trees needed fewer doses of strong pain medicine than similar patients whose windows faced a brick wall. The study took place at a hospital in Pennsylvania, and many hospitals have since planted gardens near patient wings.

Which detail best supports the idea that views of nature may aid recovery?
options: Patients facing trees needed fewer strong pain doses.
The study took place at a hospital in Pennsylvania.
Many hospitals have since planted gardens nearby.
Views of nature may do more than please the eye.
test.why: Needing less strong pain medicine is a measured sign of easier recovery, linked to the tree view.

whyNot.1: On topic but not support: where the study took place proves nothing about recovery.
whyNot.2: Shows hospitals' response, not evidence that views aid recovery.
whyNot.3: This restates the claim; it does not prove it.

explain.body: Questions often reword the passage. Scan for the idea as well as the exact word: 'physician' for 'doctor', 'yearly' for 'annual', 'older adults' for 'seniors'.

test.q:
Read the passage.

Members of the Westbrook Gym pay an annual fee of $240. Day passes cost $12, and a one-time key card costs $10.

How much does a membership cost per year?
test.why: 'Per year' matches 'annual', and the annual fee for members is $240.

whyNot.0: $10 is the one-time key card charge.
whyNot.1: $12 is the price of a day pass.
whyNot.3: This adds the other charges to the annual fee; the question asks for the membership cost per year.

explain.body: Qualifiers narrow the question: weekday or weekend, adult or child, before or after a change. The right answer matches the topic AND every qualifier.

test.q:
Read the passage.

Museum tickets cost $15 for adults and $8 for children ages 3 to 12. Children under 3 enter free. On Tuesdays after 6 p.m., admission is free for everyone.

How much will a family pay for one adult and a 5-year-old on a Tuesday at 2 p.m.?
test.why: 2 p.m. is before the free Tuesday evening hours, so normal prices apply: $15 for the adult plus $8 for a child aged 5 = $23.

whyNot.0: Free admission applies on Tuesdays after 6 p.m., not at 2 p.m.
whyNot.1: This counts the child's ticket but not the adult's.
whyNot.2: This counts the adult's ticket but not the child's; a 5-year-old is not under 3.
